las-vegas.name: CES
las-vegas.blurb: Early January. The giant consumer tech trade show takes over the Strip for four days, and big convention weeks push room rates up across town.

las-vegas.name: Spring shoulder season
las-vegas.blurb: Highs in the 70s and 80s with cooler evenings, and fewer visitors than the peak periods. Midweek stays are usually cheapest.

las-vegas.name: EDC Las Vegas
las-vegas.blurb: Mid-May. Three all-night dance music festival nights at Las Vegas Motor Speedway, north of the Strip, draw festivalgoers from out of town.

las-vegas.name: Summer heat
las-vegas.blurb: Daytime highs often top 100°F, and hotel rates run a bit higher. Plan outdoor sightseeing for early morning or after dark.

las-vegas.name: Fall shoulder season
las-vegas.blurb: The heat breaks: highs fall into the 80s and 90s, and crowds are lighter than in summer or the winter holidays.

las-vegas.name: Las Vegas Grand Prix
las-vegas.blurb: Mid-to-late November. The Formula 1 race runs on the Strip itself, with nightly road closures, detours and bus disruptions all race week.

las-vegas.name: National Finals Rodeo
las-vegas.blurb: Early-to-mid December. Ten nights of championship rodeo at the Thomas & Mack Center fill the city with rodeo fans.

las-vegas.name: New Year's Eve
las-vegas.blurb: Holiday crowds are heaviest around New Year's Eve. Book flights and hotels several weeks ahead.

chicago.name: Winter cold
chicago.blurb: Daytime highs sit in the low 30s with biting wind off the lake. Hotel and airfare rates are at their lowest, so it suits museum-focused trips.

chicago.name: St. Patrick's Day river dyeing
chicago.blurb: The Saturday before St. Patrick's Day. The Chicago River is dyed green in the morning, followed by the downtown parade; arrive early for a view.

chicago.name: Spring shoulder season
chicago.blurb: Highs from the high 50s to low 70s, reasonable hotel rates and moderate crowds. May is rainy, so pack an umbrella.

chicago.name: Summer peak season
chicago.blurb: The city's peak tourist season, with the highest hotel prices and rooms hard to find. Book three or four weeks ahead; heat waves can be humid.

chicago.name: Lollapalooza
chicago.blurb: Four days spanning the end of July and start of August in Grant Park, right by downtown and the Loop.

chicago.name: Air and Water Show
chicago.blurb: A weekend in mid-August. The free lakefront air show centers on North Avenue Beach and usually draws very large crowds.

chicago.name: Fall shoulder season
chicago.blurb: Highs in the 60s and 70s, fewer crowds and lower room rates after summer. Some outdoor attractions cut hours late in the season.

chicago.name: Chicago Marathon
chicago.blurb: Second Sunday of October. Expect street closures along the course through the city's neighborhoods.

savannah.name: Spring high season
savannah.blurb: Blooming trees and flowers and warming weather make this the most popular time to visit. Hotel rates run higher, so book ahead.

savannah.name: St. Patrick's Day
savannah.blurb: On or around March 17. One of the country's oldest St. Patrick's parades packs downtown with thousands of spectators.

savannah.name: Savannah Music Festival
savannah.blurb: Late March into early April. A 12-day festival of roots, classical and jazz concerts at venues around the historic district.

savannah.name: Summer heat and storms
savannah.blurb: Highs around 90°F with heavy humidity day and night, and frequent afternoon thunderstorms. Sightsee in the morning.

savannah.name: Peak hurricane season
savannah.blurb: Atlantic hurricane season runs June through November, with most activity from mid-August to mid-October. Consider travel insurance.

savannah.name: SCAD Savannah Film Festival
savannah.blurb: Late October. A week of film screenings hosted by the Savannah College of Art and Design.

savannah.name: Fall shoulder season
savannah.blurb: Cooler weather and slower tourism after the spring and summer high season, with the city's holiday lights starting late in the year.

san-francisco.name: J.P. Morgan Healthcare Conference
san-francisco.blurb: Mid-January. This investor conference fills hotels around Union Square, which can sell out and charge very high rates that week.

san-francisco.name: Spring
san-francisco.blurb: Mild weather with highs in the mid-60s, hotel prices that haven't yet risen for summer, and fewer tourists. Bring a layer for the wind.

san-francisco.name: Foggy summer peak
san-francisco.blurb: Peak tourist season brings higher room rates, while chilly, damp fog keeps highs in the 60s. Pack a jacket; it often isn't beach weather.

san-francisco.name: Outside Lands
san-francisco.blurb: Early-to-mid August. A three-day music festival in Golden Gate Park; expect large crowds and heavy demand on transit and taxis.

san-francisco.name: Dreamforce
san-francisco.blurb: Held in September or October at Moscone Center. Competition for hotel rooms is fierce that week and prices can soar, so book early or pick another week.

san-francisco.name: Fall warm season
san-francisco.blurb: Often the warmest, sunniest stretch of the year, with highs in the low 70s, fewer crowds and lower hotel rates than summer.

san-francisco.name: Fleet Week
san-francisco.blurb: Early-to-mid October. Navy ships visit, and the free Blue Angels air show over the Marina Green draws crowds to the waterfront.

new-york.name: Winter low season
new-york.blurb: Late January and February bring the cheapest hotel rates of the year. The trade-off is cold, with temperatures in the 20s and 30s.

new-york.name: Spring
new-york.blurb: Warming weather, outdoor markets and sidewalk dining, with highs reaching the upper 60s by May. Showers are common, so pack rain gear.

new-york.name: Summer humidity
new-york.blurb: Sticky, humid days and heavy family travel during school breaks make this one of the busiest seasons, though hotel prices stay fairly steady.

new-york.name: US Open
new-york.blurb: Late August to mid-September. The Grand Slam tennis tournament runs for two weeks at Flushing Meadows in Queens.

new-york.name: Early fall
new-york.blurb: Crisp, sunny days with highs in the 60s and 70s. One of the nicest times to walk the city, though hotels are pricier.

new-york.name: UN General Assembly
new-york.blurb: Late September. World leaders' motorcades and street closures around the UN cause gridlock on the East Side of Midtown. Allow extra travel time.

new-york.name: New York City Marathon
new-york.blurb: First Sunday of November. The race crosses all five boroughs, with street closures along the route.

new-york.name: Thanksgiving to New Year's
new-york.blurb: Thanksgiving parade crowds, then the Rockefeller Center tree and holiday windows. Hotel prices are very high through Christmas.

denver.name: National Western Stock Show
denver.blurb: About two weeks in mid-to-late January. Rodeos, livestock shows and a downtown livestock parade at the National Western Complex.

denver.name: March snowstorms
denver.blurb: March is statistically Denver's snowiest month, averaging more than 10 inches.

denver.name: Spring shoulder season
denver.blurb: Highs in the mid-50s to low 60s, fewer tourists and lower hotel prices than summer. Expect some rain.

denver.name: Summer peak season
denver.blurb: The busiest and most expensive season, with highs sometimes above 90°F and heavy July rain. Book well ahead.

denver.name: Fall shoulder season
denver.blurb: Mostly sunny days, fewer crowds and lower rates, plus many food festivals. Nights turn cold, so bring layers.

denver.name: Great American Beer Festival
denver.blurb: An October weekend. The Brewers Association's annual craft beer festival, held in Denver since 1982, draws beer fans from around the country.

austin.name: Winter quiet season
austin.blurb: Mild and dry, with highs in the low to mid-60s. It is the quietest stretch of the year and usually the cheapest.

austin.name: SXSW
austin.blurb: Mid-March, about nine days. The tech, film and music festival takes over downtown, and flight and hotel prices can rise sharply.

austin.name: Spring
austin.blurb: Highs in the 70s and 80s after SXSW clears out. Skip UT Austin's commencement weekend in May.

austin.name: Summer heat
austin.blurb: Highs in the mid- to upper 90s, sometimes over 100°F, with high humidity. Spring-fed Barton Springs Pool is the best relief.

austin.name: Austin City Limits Music Festival
austin.blurb: Two weekends in October at Zilker Park. Festival weekends bring big crowds and higher lodging rates.

austin.name: Formula 1 US Grand Prix
austin.blurb: A late-October weekend of Formula 1 racing at Circuit of the Americas, southeast of downtown.

austin.name: Late fall
austin.blurb: Daytime highs in the 70s and the fall festival rush has passed. Book a couple of months ahead for the best rates.

orlando.name: Winter low season
orlando.blurb: After the New Year rush, mild weather around 75°F, few rainy days and discounted accommodation make this the low season.

orlando.name: Spring break
orlando.blurb: March to mid-April. Spring break crowds fill the theme parks; the third week of March is often the busiest.

orlando.name: Early May lull
orlando.blurb: Crowds and prices drop between spring break and summer vacation, though highs already reach the upper 80s.

orlando.name: Summer crowds and storms
orlando.blurb: Summer vacation crowds peak, highs often top 90°F, and afternoon thunderstorms are likely. Early July is especially busy.

orlando.name: Peak hurricane season
orlando.blurb: Atlantic hurricane season runs June through November, with most activity from mid-August to mid-October. Watch forecasts and consider insurance.

orlando.name: EPCOT Food & Wine Festival
orlando.blurb: Late August to late November. Food and drink booths spread around EPCOT's World Showcase for most of the fall.

orlando.name: Pre-Christmas lull
orlando.blurb: The weeks between Thanksgiving and Christmas are quiet at the parks, with holiday decorations already up.

orlando.name: Christmas to New Year's
orlando.blurb: Christmas week through early January is one of the most crowded times at the theme parks.

charleston.name: Late fall and early winter
charleston.blurb: Highs mostly in the 50s and 60s, lighter crowds and off-season hotel deals, plus the Holiday Festival of Lights.

charleston.name: Southeastern Wildlife Exposition
charleston.blurb: A mid-February weekend. Wildlife art, dog competitions and live animal shows at venues across downtown, including Marion Square.

charleston.name: Charleston Wine + Food
charleston.blurb: Early March, five days. Dinners, tastings and a Culinary Village with chefs and winemakers from around the world.

charleston.name: Spring high season
charleston.blurb: Highs of 60 to 80°F and gardens in bloom draw heavy crowds. Hotel rates peak, especially around Easter; midweek stays help.

charleston.name: Spoleto Festival USA
charleston.blurb: Late May to early June, 17 days. An international performing arts festival with opera, theater, dance and music across the city.

charleston.name: Summer heat
charleston.blurb: Hot, humid days with highs in the upper 80s, strong sun and family vacation crowds. August is the rainiest month.

charleston.name: Peak hurricane season
charleston.blurb: Atlantic hurricane season runs June through November, with most activity from mid-August to mid-October. Consider travel insurance.

new-orleans.name: Winter lull
new-orleans.blurb: The coolest season, with highs in the 60s. Fewer tourists mean lower hotel rates, and it is the easiest time to avoid festival crowds.

new-orleans.name: Mardi Gras
new-orleans.blurb: Fat Tuesday falls between early February and early March. The week before it is the most crowded of the year, and some attractions close.

new-orleans.name: French Quarter Festival
new-orleans.blurb: Usually the second weekend of April. A free four-day music festival on stages across the French Quarter that draws large crowds.

new-orleans.name: Jazz Fest
new-orleans.blurb: Two long weekends from late April into early May at the Fair Grounds Race Course, at the height of the city's spring festival season.

new-orleans.name: Summer heat
new-orleans.blurb: The hottest and rainiest months, with highs in the low 90s and humidity that makes walking tours uncomfortable. Hotel deals are plentiful.

new-orleans.name: Essence Festival
new-orleans.blurb: Fourth of July weekend. Concerts at the Caesars Superdome plus other programming around the city.

new-orleans.name: Hurricane season peak
new-orleans.blurb: Hurricane season runs June 1 to November 30, with most activity from mid-August to mid-October. Watch forecasts and consider trip insurance.

nashville.name: Winter off-season
nashville.blurb: Cold and often gray, with temperatures from the upper 20s to the 40s, but flights and hotels are much cheaper than the rest of the year.

nashville.name: Spring
nashville.blurb: Highs start in the low 70s and warm through May. Pack for humidity and thunderstorms.

nashville.name: CMA Fest
nashville.blurb: Four days in early to mid-June. The country music festival fills downtown with fans, and hotel rates climb for the week.

nashville.name: Fourth of July
nashville.blurb: The free downtown concert and fireworks show is one of the biggest single-day events in the city, centered on Lower Broadway.

nashville.name: Summer heat
nashville.blurb: Highs reach the 90s in July, with humidity and thunderstorms, and hotel rates are at their highest in summer.

nashville.name: Fall
nashville.blurb: Temperatures ease back toward the low 70s by October, the tail end of the city's best-weather stretch.

nashville.name: A Country Christmas
nashville.blurb: Early November to early January. Gaylord Opryland's annual holiday decorations and attractions run through the holidays at the resort near the Grand Ole Opry.

nashville.name: New Year's Eve Big Bash
nashville.blurb: December 31. A free concert and countdown at Bicentennial Mall draws very large crowds. Use rideshare or shuttles.

san-diego.name: Gray whale season
san-diego.blurb: From late December to mid-March, migrating gray whales can be spotted from Cabrillo National Monument on Point Loma. It is also the cooler, rainier time of year.

san-diego.name: Spring
san-diego.blurb: Mild weather in the mid-60s and fewer crowds while school is still in session. One of the two best times to visit.

san-diego.name: May Gray and June Gloom
san-diego.blurb: A marine layer often keeps the coast cool and cloudy, sometimes all day, while crowds and room rates climb toward summer. Inland areas are usually sunnier.

san-diego.name: Summer peak
san-diego.blurb: Highs in the high 70s, but the busiest and most expensive time, with long lines at attractions and hotels that sell out. Book at least a month ahead.

san-diego.name: Comic-Con
san-diego.blurb: Late July. Downtown hotels sell out fast once Comic-Con's booking opens, and rooms near the Gaslamp get very expensive that week.

san-diego.name: Fall
san-diego.blurb: Summer weather often lasts into September. October and November bring fewer crowds and lower hotel rates.

seattle.name: Rainy season
seattle.blurb: The wet season runs roughly October through March, with November to January the wettest. Expect short gray days in the 30s and 40s, though hotel deals are plentiful.

seattle.name: Alaska cruise season
seattle.blurb: Mid-April to mid-October, cruise ships sail for Alaska from downtown piers, adding crowds downtown on sailing days.

seattle.name: Summer high season
seattle.blurb: The driest, sunniest months, with highs around 75°F. It is also the busiest time, with higher hotel rates and limited availability, so book several weeks ahead.

seattle.name: Seafair Weekend
seattle.blurb: Late July or early August. The Boeing Seafair Air Show flies over Lake Washington, with free general admission viewing at Genesee Park.

seattle.name: Early fall
seattle.blurb: Mild weather before the rains set in, smaller crowds once summer ends, and lower hotel rates. The best time to visit.

honolulu.name: Holiday high season
honolulu.blurb: Late December into early January brings the highest lodging demand of the year in Hawaii. Book early and expect higher prices.

honolulu.name: Humpback whale peak
honolulu.blurb: Humpbacks are in Hawaiian waters from about November to April, with the peak from January through March. A good time for whale-watching tours.

honolulu.name: Spring shoulder season
honolulu.blurb: Mid-April to early June is one of the cheapest and least crowded stretches for flights and hotels.

honolulu.name: Summer family season
honolulu.blurb: Mid-June to mid-August is peak family travel while schools are out, with June and July the most crowded.

honolulu.name: Fall shoulder season
honolulu.blurb: Demand usually eases after Labor Day. September to mid-November brings lower prices and quieter beaches.

honolulu.name: Thanksgiving week
honolulu.blurb: Late November. Demand for flights and rooms jumps sharply for the holiday week.

honolulu.name: Honolulu Marathon
honolulu.blurb: Mid-December, with a 5 a.m. start. Roads along the course close on race morning.

knoxville.name: Big Ears Festival
knoxville.blurb: Late March or early April. A four-day music festival spread across about two dozen downtown venues.

knoxville.name: Dogwood Arts
knoxville.blurb: April, when the dogwoods bloom along the city's marked dogwood trails. The Dogwood Arts Festival at World's Fair Park is usually late in the month.

knoxville.name: UT home football Saturdays
knoxville.blurb: Neyland Stadium seats 101,915, and campus and downtown fill with tailgaters on home Saturdays from September to November. Plan parking and arrival times ahead.

knoxville.name: Fall color downtown
knoxville.blurb: Crisp weather and changing leaves around Krutch Park and Volunteer Landing. Pick a weekend without a home football game for an easier visit.

knoxville.name: Holidays on Ice
knoxville.blurb: The Market Square skating rink runs from late November to early January, closed Christmas Day.

asheville.name: January lull
asheville.blurb: One of the least busy months, with affordable hotel rates. It is also the snowiest month, with temperatures in the 30s, and mountain roads can be tricky.

asheville.name: Biltmore Blooms
asheville.blurb: Late March to late May. Tulips, daffodils, azaleas and wisteria fill the Biltmore Estate gardens and house.

asheville.name: Mountain Dance and Folk Festival
asheville.blurb: Late July into early August. Three evenings of traditional mountain music and dance, held every summer since 1928.

asheville.name: Fall leaf season
asheville.blurb: October is the busiest month. Colors peak in the city in the second half of the month, rooms book early and rates are at their highest.

asheville.name: Christmas at Biltmore
asheville.blurb: Early November to early January. Daytime visits need a timed reservation, and Candlelight Christmas Evenings need a separate ticket booked ahead.

daytona-beach.name: Daytona 500 and Speedweeks
daytona-beach.blurb: Mid to late February. Speedweeks races lead up to the Daytona 500, held on a Sunday.

daytona-beach.name: Bike Week
daytona-beach.blurb: Ten days from late February into early March. Big motorcycle crowds fill the area and overlap with spring breakers.

daytona-beach.name: April
daytona-beach.blurb: Warm, sunny days with highs around 81°F, after the February and March event crowds have gone.

daytona-beach.name: Coke Zero Sugar 400
daytona-beach.blurb: Late August. A Saturday night NASCAR Cup race at Daytona International Speedway.

daytona-beach.name: Hurricane season peak
daytona-beach.blurb: Hurricane season runs June 1 to November 30, with most activity from mid-August to mid-October. Watch forecasts and consider trip insurance.

daytona-beach.name: Biketoberfest
daytona-beach.blurb: Four days in mid-October. A large motorcycle rally with events across Volusia County.

daytona-beach.name: November
daytona-beach.blurb: Highs around 77°F and one of the better months for weather, after Biketoberfest and before winter.

key-west.name: Winter high season
key-west.blurb: The busiest and most expensive time, with temperatures in the mid-70s. Holiday weeks add even more visitors.

key-west.name: Spring
key-west.blurb: Winter crowds thin out, hotel rates are more reasonable, and skies are clear, with highs climbing to the mid-80s by May. The best time to visit.

key-west.name: Key West Pride
key-west.blurb: Early June, with a street fair and several days of events. Room rates surge during Pride.

key-west.name: Hemingway Days
key-west.blurb: The week of Hemingway's July 21 birthday, with the look-alike contest at Sloppy Joe's, a fishing contest and a street fair.

key-west.name: Lobster mini-season
key-west.blurb: The last Wednesday and Thursday of July. Thousands of locals and visitors take to the water for the two-day spiny lobster sport season.

key-west.name: Hurricane season peak
key-west.blurb: Hurricane season runs June 1 to November 30, with most activity from mid-August to mid-October. Watch forecasts and consider trip insurance.

key-west.name: Fantasy Fest
key-west.blurb: Ten days in late October, ending with the main parade. An adults-first event; Old Town hotels sell out months ahead and rates rise toward parade weekend.

miami.name: Miami Marathon
miami.blurb: Run on a Sunday in late January or early February. Streets in Downtown, Coconut Grove and Miami Beach close from about 5 a.m. to 2 p.m. on race day.

miami.name: Calle Ocho Festival
miami.blurb: A one-day street festival in mid-March that closes 15 blocks of SW 8th Street in Little Havana. Great if you want to go; plan around it if you're staying nearby.

miami.name: Miami Open
miami.blurb: The pro tennis tournament runs for about two weeks in the second half of March at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens.

miami.name: Miami Music Week and Ultra
miami.blurb: Late March brings a week of 200-plus electronic music events, ending with the three-day Ultra festival at Bayfront Park in Downtown Miami.

miami.name: Formula 1 Miami Grand Prix
miami.blurb: Race weekend falls around the turn of April and May at the Miami International Autodrome on the Hard Rock Stadium campus in Miami Gardens.

miami.name: Rainy season
miami.blurb: South Florida's wet season runs from mid-May to mid-October, with hot, humid days and frequent thunderstorms.

miami.name: Miami Spice
miami.blurb: Through August and September, 300-plus restaurants offer three-course prix-fixe menus, a good way to eat well during the slower, hotter months.

miami.name: Hurricane season peak
miami.blurb: Hurricane season runs June 1 to November 30, and most Atlantic activity falls between mid-August and mid-October. Buy flexible bookings or travel insurance.

miami-beach.name: Miami International Boat Show
miami-beach.blurb: A five-day show in mid-February at the Miami Beach Convention Center and marinas on both sides of Biscayne Bay.

miami-beach.name: South Beach Wine & Food Festival
miami-beach.blurb: Four days of chef-led tastings and dinners across South Beach in late February. Book early if you're coming for it.

miami-beach.name: Spring break
miami-beach.blurb: In March, South Beach has used non-resident garage rates of $40 or more, beach-entrance checkpoints Thursday to Sunday, and limits on Ocean Drive traffic.

miami-beach.name: Miami Beach Pride
miami-beach.blurb: A week of events in April that ends with a festival at Lummus Park and a parade along Ocean Drive.

miami-beach.name: Memorial Day weekend
miami-beach.blurb: The city has used flat garage rates for non-residents, nightly lane reductions on 5th Street and the Julia Tuttle, and license plate readers on this weekend.

miami-beach.name: Sargassum season
miami-beach.blurb: Sargassum seaweed can wash up from March through October, usually heaviest in late spring and summer. The amount varies a lot from year to year.

miami-beach.name: Art Basel Miami Beach
miami-beach.blurb: The art fair is held in Miami Beach in early December and is the centerpiece of Miami Art Week. Book rooms early if you're coming for it.

miami-beach.name: Dry season
miami-beach.blurb: After the wet season ends in mid-October, the weather turns drier and less humid. These months are the most comfortable for the beach.

key-biscayne.name: Winter weekdays
key-biscayne.blurb: Crandon Park Beach is much less crowded in winter, and on weekdays you may have long stretches of sand nearly to yourself.

key-biscayne.name: Sargassum season
key-biscayne.blurb: Miami-Dade's sargassum season runs from March through October, and the island's ocean-facing beaches can get heavy seaweed in some years.

key-biscayne.name: Rainy season
key-biscayne.blurb: From mid-May to mid-October, expect heat, humidity and frequent thunderstorms. Plan beach time for the morning.

key-biscayne.name: Summer weekend crowds
key-biscayne.blurb: On summer weekends, Crandon Park's 3,000 parking spaces fill up and shaded picnic tables go early. Come on a weekday or arrive early.

key-biscayne.name: Fourth of July Parade
key-biscayne.blurb: Held every July 4 since 1959, the morning parade runs along Crandon Boulevard, the island's main road.

key-biscayne.name: Hurricane season peak
key-biscayne.blurb: Most Atlantic hurricane activity comes between mid-August and mid-October. The Rickenbacker Causeway is the only road on and off the island.

fort-lauderdale.name: Spring break
fort-lauderdale.blurb: Spring break rules on the beach run from March into mid-April. Alcohol, coolers, tents and amplified music are banned, and police patrols increase.

fort-lauderdale.name: Tortuga Music Festival
fort-lauderdale.blurb: A three-day music festival on Fort Lauderdale Beach Park in early April.

fort-lauderdale.name: Fort Lauderdale Air Show
fort-lauderdale.blurb: An air show over Fort Lauderdale Beach on a weekend in mid-May, with crowds along the sand.

fort-lauderdale.name: Rainy season
fort-lauderdale.blurb: From mid-May to mid-October, expect heat, humidity and near-daily thunderstorms.

fort-lauderdale.name: Dine Out Lauderdale
fort-lauderdale.blurb: Dine Out Lauderdale, a restaurant promotion, runs in August and September. It makes late summer a better-value time to eat out.

fort-lauderdale.name: Hurricane season peak
fort-lauderdale.blurb: Hurricane season runs June to November, and most activity falls between mid-August and mid-October.

fort-lauderdale.name: Fort Lauderdale International Boat Show
fort-lauderdale.blurb: Held at six waterfront venues from late October into the first days of November, with shuttles from the Broward County Convention Center.

fort-lauderdale.name: Winterfest Boat Parade
fort-lauderdale.blurb: A lighted holiday boat parade through Fort Lauderdale on a Saturday in mid-December.

tampa.name: Gasparilla Parade of Pirates
tampa.blurb: On a Saturday in late January, a 4.5-mile pirate parade runs down Bayshore Boulevard into downtown. It's free and draws big crowds.

tampa.name: Florida State Fair
tampa.blurb: The state fair runs for about 12 days in early to mid-February at the Florida State Fairgrounds in Tampa.

tampa.name: Yankees spring training
tampa.blurb: The Yankees play Grapefruit League games at Steinbrenner Field from late February until about the third week of March.

tampa.name: Rainy season
tampa.blurb: From late May to early October, expect frequent thunderstorms. The peak, with heavy rain and frequent lightning, runs from July to early September.

tampa.name: Red tide risk
tampa.blurb: Red tide blooms appear most years in late summer or early fall, often between Clearwater and Sanibel. They can cause eye and breathing irritation at the beach.

tampa.name: Hurricane season peak
tampa.blurb: Hurricane season runs June 1 to November 30, and most Atlantic activity falls between mid-August and mid-October.

tampa.name: Late fall
tampa.blurb: The rainy season ends around early October, so late fall brings drier weather before the January Gasparilla crowds.

st-augustine.name: Celtic Music & Heritage Festival
st-augustine.blurb: A weekend festival of Celtic music and culture in mid-March at Francis Field, downtown.

st-augustine.name: Spring
st-augustine.blurb: From March through mid-May the weather is usually pleasant, which suits walking the old town and visiting the Castillo.

st-augustine.name: Summer heat and storms
st-augustine.blurb: Summers are hot and humid with frequent afternoon thunderstorms. The heat index inside the Castillo can top 105°F, and lightning closes its gundeck.

st-augustine.name: Hurricane season peak
st-augustine.blurb: Hurricane season runs June 1 to November 30, and most Atlantic activity falls between mid-August and mid-October.

st-augustine.name: King tides
st-augustine.blurb: Fall king tides can flood low streets, including near the bayfront seawall by the Castillo and parts of Bridge Street. Check tide times if you're driving downtown.

st-augustine.name: Autumn
st-augustine.blurb: October through late November is often mild and pleasant, after the summer heat and before the holiday lights crowds.

st-augustine.name: Nights of Lights
st-augustine.blurb: Millions of white lights stay on nightly from late November to mid-January. Traffic and parking are hard on weekends, so come midweek if you can.

st-augustine.name: Colonial Night Watch
st-augustine.blurb: On the first weekend in December, reenactors camp in town and a torch-lit parade moves down St. George Street on Saturday night.

fort-myers.name: Peak season
fort-myers.blurb: Lee County's peak season typically runs from mid-January through April. Book lodging well ahead.

fort-myers.name: Edison Festival of Light
fort-myers.blurb: A February festival in Fort Myers that ends with the evening Grand Parade of Light in mid-to-late February.

fort-myers.name: Spring training
fort-myers.blurb: From late February to late March, the Red Sox play at JetBlue Park and the Twins at Hammond Stadium.

fort-myers.name: Spring break on Fort Myers Beach
fort-myers.blurb: March is one of the busiest months on Fort Myers Beach. Expect heavy traffic onto Estero Island and beachfront hotels booked weeks out.

fort-myers.name: Summer off-season
fort-myers.blurb: Summer is the low season. It's hot and humid, with tropical thunderstorms most afternoons.

fort-myers.name: Red tide risk
fort-myers.blurb: Red tide blooms appear most years in late summer or early fall, often between Clearwater and Sanibel. They can cause eye and breathing irritation at the beach.

fort-myers.name: Hurricane season peak
fort-myers.blurb: Hurricane season runs June 1 to November 30, and most Atlantic activity falls between mid-August and mid-October.

fort-myers.name: Fall shelling season
fort-myers.blurb: October and November bring good shelling on nearby Sanibel, with less rain and lighter crowds than winter. Hurricane season runs through November.

sarasota.name: Winter high season
sarasota.blurb: Most of Sarasota's visitors and snowbirds arrive in winter, when highs sit in the 60s and 70s. This is the area's peak season.

sarasota.name: Forks & Corks
sarasota.blurb: The Forks & Corks food and wine Grand Tasting is held on a Sunday in late January at The Ringling museum.

sarasota.name: Orioles spring training
sarasota.blurb: The Orioles play home games at Ed Smith Stadium from late February to mid-March.

sarasota.name: Summer rainy season
sarasota.blurb: From June to October, downpours are common, usually in the early afternoon. They pass quickly, but lightning can linger.

sarasota.name: Red tide risk
sarasota.blurb: Red tide blooms appear most years in late summer or early fall along this stretch of coast. They can cause eye and breathing irritation on the beaches.

sarasota.name: Hurricane season peak
sarasota.blurb: Hurricane season runs June 1 to November 30, and its prime time locally is August and September.

sarasota.name: Fall shoulder season
sarasota.blurb: Fall is a shoulder season with mild weather and little rain, after summer storms and before the winter rush.

sarasota.name: Siesta Key Crystal Classic
sarasota.blurb: An international sand-sculpting contest on Siesta Key Beach over four days in mid-November.

naples.name: Peak season
naples.blurb: December through April is Naples' peak season. Book rooms and restaurant tables early.

naples.name: Naples Winter Wine Festival
naples.blurb: A charity wine auction weekend in late January at The Ritz-Carlton Naples, Tiburón, during an already busy month.

naples.name: Naples National Art Fair
naples.blurb: A juried art fair in Cambier Park, downtown Naples, over a weekend in late February.

naples.name: Summer off-season
naples.blurb: May through September brings fewer crowds and lower hotel rates, at the cost of more heat and humidity.

naples.name: Rainy season
naples.blurb: South Florida's wet season runs from mid-May to mid-October, with frequent afternoon thunderstorms.

naples.name: Hurricane season peak
naples.blurb: Hurricane season runs June 1 to November 30, and most Atlantic activity falls between mid-August and mid-October.

naples.name: Stone Crab Festival
naples.blurb: A late-October festival in Tin City that celebrates the new stone crab season, which opens October 15.

naples.name: Stone crab season
naples.blurb: Florida's stone crab season runs from October 15 through May 1, the only time fresh claws are on local menus.
